content: 1. The study titled Patients’ Perspectives: Italy as a Case Study published in the European Journal of Health Economics in 2016 (Volume 17, Issue 8, Pages 963–977) explores the viewpoints of patients in Italy regarding healthcare policies and their implications. 2. Schneeweiss et al. (2004) investigated the net health plan savings achieved through reference pricing for angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors among elderly residents in British Columbia. Their findings were published in Medical Care (Volume 42, Issue 7, Pages 653–660). 3. Andersson et al. (2006) analyzed the effects of policy changes in pharmaceutical reimbursement schedules on drug expenditures in Sweden from 1986 to 2002. This interrupted time series analysis was published in Health Policy (Volume 79, Issues 2–3, Pages 231–243). 4. Leopold et al. (2014) examined the impact of pharmaceutical policy interventions on the utilization of antipsychotic medications in Finland and Portugal during economic recessions. Their interrupted time series analyses were published in the International Journal for Equity in Health (Volume 13, Issue 1, Pages 1–9). 5. Von der Schulenburg, Vandoros, and Kanavos (2011) reviewed the effects of drug market regulation on pharmaceutical prices in Europe, with a focus on ACE inhibitors. Their findings were published in Health Economics Review. 6. Grootendorst et al. (2005) studied the impact of reference pricing for nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents on the use and costs of analgesic drugs. Their research appeared in Health Services Research (Volume 40, Issue 5I, Pages 1297–1317). 7. Acosta et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review on the effects of reference pricing, other pricing, and purchasing policies on pharmaceutical markets. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 8. Dylst, Vulto, and Simoens (2011) reviewed the impact of reference-pricing systems in Europe through a literature review and case studies. Their work was published in the Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research (Volume 11, Issue 6, Pages 729–737). 9. Galizzi, Ghislandi, and Miraldo (2011) reviewed the effects of reference pricing in pharmaceutical markets. Their findings were published in PharmacoEconomics (Volume 29, Issue 1, Pages 17–33). 10. Puig-Junoy (2005) discussed the requirements for evaluating the impact of pharmaceutical reference pricing in Applied Health Economics and Health Policy (Volume 4, Issue 2, Pages 87–98). 11. Kaplan et al. (2016) explored policy options for promoting the use of generic medicines in lowand middle-income countries. Their report was published in March 2016. 12. The 2015 Global Survey on Health Technology Assessment by National Authorities provided insights into the global landscape of health technology assessment practices. 13. Ben-Aharon, Shavit, and Magnezi (2017) examined the effects of drug price regulation on healthcare expenditures in the European Journal of Health Economics (Volume 18, Issue 7, Pages 859–867). 14. Kwon et al. (2011) analyzed the impact of price cuts on drug spending in South Korea, focusing on antihyperlipidemic agents. Their findings were published in Health Policy. 15. Salas-Vega, Bertling, and Mossialos (2016) conducted a comparative study of drug listing recommendations and decision-making processes in Australia, the Netherlands, Sweden, and the UK. Their research appeared in Health Policy (Volume 120, Issue 10, Pages 1104–1114). 16. Akehurst et al. (2017) reviewed variations in health technology assessment and reimbursement processes across Europe. Their findings were published in Value in Health (Volume 20, Issue 1, Pages 67–76). 17. Harris (2005) critiqued discriminatory practices in healthcare decision-making in the Journal of Medical Ethics (Volume 31, Pages 373–375). 18. Nord, Daniels, and Kamlet (2009) discussed challenges associated with quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) in Value in Health (Volume 12, Supplement). 19. Caro et al. (2018) debated the direction of health technology assessment in determining value in PharmacoEconomics. 20. Rajan, Gutierrez-Ibarluzea, and Moharra (2011) addressed issues in promoting health technology assessment, including motives, enablers, and barriers, in the International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care (Volume 27, Issue 1, Pages 55–63). 21. Cueny (2018) discussed pricing and market development strategies in the pharmaceutical industry in Pharma Boardroom. 22. Tsevat and Moriates (2018) explored the intersection of value-based healthcare and cost-effectiveness analysis in the Annals of Internal Medicine (Volume 169, Issue 5, Pages 329–332). 23. Abdel Rida et al. (2017) conducted a systematic review of pharmaceutical pricing policies in developing countries, published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Services Research (Volume 8, Issue 4, Pages 213–226). 24. The WHO Collaborating Centre for Pharmaceutical Pricing and Reimbursement Policies published a country poster book in 2015, addressing challenges beyond the financial crisis. 25. Cheng et al. (2012) studied the effects of the zero mark-up policy on medicines in Beijing community health facilities, published in Pharm Policy Law (Volume 14, Issues 2–4, Pages 177–186). 26. Fu, Li, and Yip (2007) examined the intended and unintended impacts of price changes for drugs and medical services in China, published in Social Science & Medicine. 27. Yang et al. (2017) analyzed the impact of the zero-markup drug policy on hospitalization expenditures in rural China, published in Tropical Medicine & International Health (Volume 22, Issue 2, Pages 180–186). 28. Zhou et al. (2015) evaluated the financial impact of the Zero-Markup Policy for Essential Drugs on patients in county hospitals in rural China, published in PLoS One (Volume 10, Issue 3). 29. Li et al. (2008) assessed the effects of implementing the Without Added Profit policy in Chengdu community health service institutions, published in the Chinese Journal of New Drugs. 30. Bhaskarabhatla et al. (2017) studied the regulatory impact of partial price controls on metformin in India, published in Health Policy and Planning (Volume 32, Issue 2, Pages 194–204). 31. Lu et al. (2013) analyzed changes in the use of antidiabetic medications following price regulations in China, published in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Health Services Research (Volume 4, Issue 1, Pages 3–11). 32. Chu, Liu, and Romeis (2011) assessed the effects of drug price reduction policies on older people in Taiwan, published in Health Services Management Research (Volume 24, Issue 1, Pages 1–7). 33. The 72nd World Health Assembly in 2019 addressed improving transparency in markets for medicines, vaccines, and other health products. 34. Véran (2019) proposed Amendment No. 474, addressing pharmaceutical pricing and transparency. 35. The Council of the European Communities issued a directive in 1988 on the transparency of measures regulating the pricing of medicinal products for human use. 36. Pauwels et al. (2017) reviewed managed entry agreements for oncology drugs in Europe, published in Frontiers in Pharmacology (Volume 8). 37. Moodley and Suleman (2019) evaluated the impact of South Africa's single exit price policy on originator medicines, published in BMC Health Services Research (Volume 19, Issue 1). 38. Langley et al. (2018) evaluated a price transparency intervention for commonly prescribed medications, published in Future Healthcare Journal (Volume 5, Issue 3, Pages 198–202). 39. Berdud et al. (2018) discussed global health procurement and pricing transparency issues. 40. Moon (2018) advocated for removing opacity in medicine pricing in the British Medical Journal. 41. Kyle and Ridley (2007) examined whether greater transparency and uniformity in healthcare prices would benefit poor patients, published in Health Affairs (Volume 26, Issue 5, Pages 1384–1391). 42. Kohler and Dimancesco (2020) analyzed the risk of corruption in public pharmaceutical procurement and the role of anti-corruption measures, published in Global Health Action. 43. Kahn (2019) reported on pharmaceutical manufacturers' resistance to transparency in medicine pricing. 44. The Association of American Medical Colleges addressed price transparency in teaching hospitals. 45. Maniadakis et al. (2018) explored pharmaceutical tendering for effectiveness and sustainability in countries with expanding healthcare coverage. 46. Garattini, Van de Vooren, and Freemantle (2014) discussed lessons from Italy on tendering and value-based pricing for HPV vaccines, published in the Journal of the Royal Society of Medicine (Volume 107, Issue 1, Pages 4–5). 47. Adesina, Wirtz, and Dratler (2013) reviewed Mexico's experience in reforming antiretroviral price negotiations and public procurement, published in Health Policy and Planning (Volume 28, Issue 1). 48. Clark et al. (2014) evaluated the impact of a value-based benefits program targeting generic medications, published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy (Volume 20, Issue 2, Pages 141–150). 49. Fraeyman et al. (2013) analyzed co-payment and generic market share trends in Belgium's reference pricing system, published in Applied Health Economics and Health Policy (Volume 11, Issue 5, Pages 543–552). 50. Chen et al. (2008) studied the effects of Taiwan's generic grouping price policy on drug prices and expenditures, published in BMC Public Health (Volume 8). 51. Godman et al. (2013) examined initiatives in Sweden to enhance ARB prescribing efficiency, published in the International Journal of Clinical Practice (Volume 67, Issue 9, Pages 853–862). 52. Lee et al. (2013) evaluated the success of Argentina's generic drug law, published in Value in Health (Volume 16, Issue 7). 53. Bhargava et al. (2010) assessed the impact of generic medication vouchers on dispensing ratios, published in the Journal of Managed Care Pharmacy (Volume 16, Issue 6, Pages 384–392). 54. Danzon and Furukawa (2010) provided cross-national evidence on generic pharmaceuticals in pharmacyvs. physician-driven markets. 55. Balmaceda, Espinoza, and Diaz (2010) analyzed the impact of therapeutic equivalence policies on medicine prices in Chile. 56. An editorial in The Lancet Rheumatology (2019) discussed the complexities of biosimilar use in the USA. 57. The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania addressed legal issues related to pharmaceutical pricing. 58. Colgan et al. (2015) reviewed perceptions of generic medications among the general population, doctors, and pharmacists, published in BMJ Open. 59. Gebresillassie et al. (2018) evaluated perceptions of generic medicines in Gondar town, Ethiopia, published in PLoS One. 60. Jacobs et al. (2016) conducted an international survey on patient attitudes and understanding of biosimilars, published in Patient Preference and Adherence.
